leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eleven members explicitly prefer B009 as their single configuration, but they do not name the same laureates. Five propose Autor, Hanson and Katz (Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell). Two propose Autor, Dorn and Hanson (Dreber Almenberg, Teorell). So no identical three-name configuration has six explicit supporters in round 1. What is shared: Autor and Hanson appear in all seven proposals, the foundational work is mature (roughly 1992 to 2016), and the designs are replicated and transparent. What is not shared: whether the discovery is the combined technology and trade account of labour demand (Katz kept, Dorn dropped) or the China-shock evidence and local adjustment (Dorn kept, Katz dropped). The citations also differ in breadth. Several supporters say they would accept the other trio if the committee defined the discovery differently (Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Teorell), but these are conditional statements and not counted as preferences. Four non-supporters (Andersson, Boppart, Friberg, Strömberg) name B009 as an alternative, so every member either prefers it or lists it as an alternative. Three of the four give reasons for ranking it below their first choice: bundling of two strands, overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes, and Dorn's omission under the three-name cap.

Three members explicitly prefer B014, all with the two-name set Melitz and Helpman, and all describe a single, compact discovery (firm heterogeneity, selection into exporting and FDI, reallocation). Their citations differ somewhat in emphasis. They stress maturity of over twenty years, repeated testing on firm-level data, and wide use in trade, macro and IO. Ten members either prefer B014 or list it as an alternative (all except Dreber Almenberg, who ranked it sixth and questions priority, Krugman's 2008 overlap and welfare-gain size). The supporters themselves concede the same reservations: priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn; the size of welfare gains under the Arkolakis-Costinot-Rodriguez-Clare critique; overlap with Krugman 2008; and the split of Helpman's credit with B049. They differ in how far these reservations qualify the case and propose wording around selection and reallocation. They also exclude Redding, who is credited on the list.

One member explicitly prefers B045, with Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn credited for estimation of demand, market power and competition in differentiated-product industries. His case rests on thirty years of scrutiny, wide transfer beyond IO, use in merger review, and a relatively clean BLP attribution. Dreber Almenberg, Fredriksson and Friberg list B045 as an alternative, so it has some cross-member recognition, but no other member prefers it in round 1. He acknowledges that the three-name cap excludes Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, that the demand-side and dynamic-industry contributions are related but distinct, and that the case is largely methodological. He also keeps B009 and B014 as strong alternatives and concedes B009's Dorn-or-Katz attribution problem.

areas_of_agreement: B009 and B014 are treated as mature, scientifically strong candidates by nearly all members. Every member either prefers B009 or lists it as an alternative, and ten of eleven prefer or list B014.
In every B009 proposal Autor and Hanson are credited. All proposals for B014 on the shortlist name Helpman and Melitz, and the three B014 supporters exclude Redding.

Members agree that the core B009 work has been replicated and scrutinised for more than a decade, and that debate over shift-share inference, persistence and external validity concerns magnitudes more than the existence of local adjustment costs.
Members agree that the overlap of B009 with the 2023 and 2024 prizes must be addressed in the citation wording, although they describe what those prizes covered in somewhat different terms.
Members agree that the task-based theory should not be claimed by a B009 citation, since Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo are not credited.

B050 is not preferred by anyone after round 1. Its opening first-place supporter, Hjalmarsson, now prefers B009 and treats B050 as an alternative for a later year because of maturity and attribution within a large team.
B040 is not preferred by anyone after round 1. Hassler moved from B040 to B009 and keeps B040 as an alternative, and Enflo and Strömberg also list it as an alternative.
scientific_disputes: B009: whether the technology and wage-structure strand and the trade-shock strand are one achievement (the five Autor-Hanson-Katz supporters lean this way) or two separable discoveries (several members raise this risk, including Boppart and Friberg).

B009: how much weight to give the shift-share exposure-design inference debate and the persistence and external validity of the China-shock estimates, compared with the long-confirmed skill-premium evidence.

B009 versus B040: Krusell, Teorell and Fredriksson argue that B040 relies on cross-country constitutional variation sensitive to specification and overlaps with the 2024 institutions prize. Hassler, in opening, argued that B040 has concentrated attribution and full maturity.

B014: whether the heterogeneous-firm framework is a discovery or a theoretical refinement of Krugman's earlier work, and how much of the welfare-gain claim survives the Arkolakis-Costinot-Rodriguez-Clare critique. Friberg and Boppart argue it qualifies the citation, while Dreber Almenberg and Strömberg weigh it more heavily.
B045: whether a methodological advance should be weighed differently from a discovery-based candidate (Andersson says no, Krusell had asked), and whether identification critiques of BLP matter.
Field balance as an argument: Fredriksson notes that trade has not been recognised since 2008. Boppart says he does not rest his case on it, and Strömberg treats it as distinct from merit.
attribution_disputes: B009: Dorn or Katz as the third name. Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson and Krusell prefer Katz as anchor of the long-run wage-structure evidence. Dreber Almenberg and Teorell prefer Dorn as a full co-author of the China-shock papers. Both sides concede the cost of the omitted name, and the three-name cap forces the choice.
B009: contributions of Levy and Murnane, and of Acemoglu and Restrepo on the theory side, are not credited. Members differ in how far this limits the citation to the empirical contribution.

B009 and B050: Katz appears on both ballot entries. Enflo, Fredriksson and Hassler discuss whether this implies double counting, and Fredriksson sees no real overlap because the roles differ. Hassler notes the committee has not settled how credit divides.

B014: priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn are not credited on this line. Supporters argue that Melitz's model is distinct, while Dreber Almenberg and Hjalmarsson treat this as the main weakness. Helpman's credit is also split with the separate B049 candidacy, and Friberg and Strömberg argue the two rationales are separable.
B014: Redding is credited on the list but left out by all three supporters as a later consolidator, which Andersson notes would blur the core-discovery rationale if added.
B045: the three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. It is also unclear whether demand estimation and Pakes's dynamic-industry work form one coherent citation.
B050: proposals differ among Chetty alone (Strömberg), Chetty and Hendren (Hjalmarsson), and Chetty, Friedman and Hendren (Enflo), which shows the credit boundary within a large team is unsettled.
B040: Krusell proposes Persson and Tabellini only, while the other six B040 proposals add Besley.
maturity_disputes: B009: the foundational work spans the early 1990s to the mid-2010s and is regarded as mature by its supporters. The residual question is whether the trade-shock magnitudes and persistence are settled enough to anchor a citation.

B050: Enflo, Fredriksson, Dreber Almenberg and Hjalmarsson all see the main results (about 2014 onward) as less mature, with neighbourhood-effect interpretation and cross-country replication still being tested. Hjalmarsson accepts this and treats B050 as a candidate for a later year.
B014 and B045: members judge them mature (more than twenty and about thirty years respectively). The disputes are about attribution and priority, not maturity.
B009 relative to recent prizes: the dispute is less about age of the work than about how much marginal recognition remains after the 2023 and 2024 prizes.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler): disclosed co-authorship and IIES ties to Krusell, Boppart and Friberg. None is a credited name on the shortlist. In opening, the chair flagged a possible Stockholm proximity of some B040 candidates that the supplied profile does not document, and B040 is now only an alternative. Disclosed and not adjudicated.

Friberg: co-authored an IJIO 2026 paper with the chair and with Tore Ellingsen. His work on exchange-rate pass-through is adjacent to B014 and B011. He also discloses that his spouse is a Swedish politician, a public fact with no stated bearing on any shortlisted achievement. Friberg prefers B014.

Boppart: long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow, who is credited in B031, an alternative Boppart lists. He also notes co-authorship with Krusell and Hassler. Boppart prefers B014, and neither Melitz nor Helpman is a stated co-author.

Krusell: his capital-skill complementarity work is in the same literature as B009, though none of its co-authors is a proposed laureate. He is a frequent co-author of the chair and a co-author of Boppart. Krusell prefers B009.

Fredriksson: shares empirical labour-economics methods with B009 candidates but reports no documented tie. He notes institutional overlap with the IIES macro group (Hassler, Krusell). Fredriksson prefers B009.
Teorell: field proximity to B040 (political institutions), which he lists in opening but not as an alternative. Teorell prefers B009 and reports no tie to Autor, Hanson or Dorn.
Enflo: B040 is adjacent to her work on railroads and the state. She reports no personal connection to its credited names, and B040 is an alternative for her.
Andersson: SSE affiliation shared with Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, described as collegial and not a tie to any B045 candidate.
Strömberg: adjunct appointment at Chicago Booth, reported as not linked to B014, B009 or B040 candidates.

Dreber Almenberg and Hjalmarsson: no conflicts apparent for their preferred or alternative parts. Dreber Almenberg's co-authors are in behavioural and metascience research, and Hjalmarsson's frequent co-authors are not credited on any shortlisted entry.
All connections are as stated in the members' own notes and the supplied profiles. They are disclosed and not adjudicated, and no independent verification is claimed.
questions_for_round2: B009: should the committee define the achievement as the combined technology and trade account of labour demand and wage inequality (Autor, Hanson, Katz) or as the China-shock and local adjustment evidence (Autor, Dorn, Hanson)? Could Dreber Almenberg and Teorell state whether they would prefer the Katz trio if the broader definition were adopted, and could Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson and Krusell state whether they would prefer the Dorn trio if the narrower definition were adopted?

B009: can the members draft one concrete citation for each trio and test whether it credits only the empirical contribution and avoids claiming the task-based theory, given Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo are not credited?

B009: what does each member consider the 2023 and 2024 prizes to have recognised, and does that make the overlap with B009 thematic only or does it reduce the marginal contribution? Statements in round 1 describe those prizes differently.

B009 versus B014: Boppart, Friberg and Strömberg should say what evidence would lead them to prefer B009, and the B009 supporters should say what would lead them to prefer B014. Specifically, how do the priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn, and the Arkolakis-Costinot-Rodriguez-Clare critique, compare with the Dorn-or-Katz and bundling issues in B009?

B014: Dreber Almenberg asked how Boppart weighs Krugman 2008, the uncredited priority claims and welfare-gain size against the framework's reach. Could Boppart, Friberg and Strömberg answer directly, and could they say whether a citation limited to selection and reallocation resolves the priority issue?

B045: can Andersson say whether the committee should treat a methods contribution like BLP by the same criteria as a discovery-based candidate, and whether a Bresnahan-inclusive configuration would change his preference? Do Dreber Almenberg, Fredriksson and Friberg, who list B045 as an alternative, see any configuration in which it would become their preferred part?

Configuration: if neither B009 trio can be settled, would any member prefer a configuration spanning more than one ballot entry, and how should credit be divided under the three-laureate limit? Should B040 or B050 remain in discussion given that no member now prefers them?
summary.chair_observation: After round 1, seven of eleven members explicitly prefer B009, three prefer B014 and one prefers B045. The B009 support is split on the laureate set, five for Autor, Hanson and Katz and two for Autor, Dorn and Hanson, so no identical configuration has the six votes a majority requires. The B014 position is the most uniform in attribution, with Melitz and Helpman named in every shortlist proposal, but it has three explicit supporters and its supporters acknowledge unresolved priority and welfare-gain questions. The main open issue for round 2 is therefore the definition of the B009 discovery and the resulting Dorn-or-Katz choice, followed by how B009 and B014 compare on attribution. The chair's own round-1 position is among the five supporters of Autor, Hanson and Katz, and the chair moved from B040 first in opening to B009 after reading colleagues. This summary describes stated positions and is not a ruling, and no hidden votes are inferred.
